📡 Offline Ops — Export / Import

Use this if the producer can't see your logs (connection or Supabase issue) and asks you to send your data across directly — e.g. via AirDrop or WhatsApp. This downloads everything logged on this device as one file; it doesn't need a connection to work.
Once downloaded, send the file to your producer — they'll import it on their end and it'll merge in correctly without creating duplicates, even if you export more than once.

📥 Import Setup from Producer

Use this if there's no internet at all at this venue, or Supabase is down, and the producer can't publish the draw sheet / pars / rosters the normal way. They'll send you a "Setup Package" file directly (AirDrop/USB/local file share) — pick it below to load the draw sheet, course pars/yardages, camera roster, and playoff roster straight onto this device so you can keep logging.
This fully replaces this device's current draw sheet/pars/rosters with what's in the file — only import a file you know is the latest from your producer.

📦 Emergency Local Backup — use if Supabase itself is down for a while Show ▾
Logging itself never stops for a connection problem — every shot is saved on this device the instant it's logged and queued to sync automatically once the connection is back (see the 📴 badge in the header when that's happening). This section is for the longer, rarer case: Supabase's own servers are down (not just this device's wifi), possibly for hours, and you need to get your data out of this one device in the meantime.

Every export already works fully offline. Editor PDF, EDL, SGFX/Rounds Payoff/L3 Info CSVs, and Export All Cameras all build entirely in this browser from whatever this device currently has in memory — none of them need Supabase at export time. As long as this device's shot log and playlists are up to date, you can keep exporting normally even during an outage.

For a full safety copy of everything on this device (shot log, playlists, draw sheet groups, camera/playoff rosters, course pars/yardages, OOM standings, Rounds Payoff, EDL settings) — download a backup file any time, with no connection required:


To restore a backup — e.g. onto a fresh device, or to push a device's offline work back once Supabase is reachable again — pick the JSON file below. This merges into whatever's already loaded (nothing already newer is overwritten) and, if online, saves straight to Supabase; if still offline, it queues the same way any other change does.
Tip: select multiple backup files at once (one per device) to merge them all in one go, correctly ordered by timecode — e.g. Cmd/Ctrl+click each device’s file in the picker.

📦 Publish Setup via File Show ▾

For a venue with no internet at all (or a Supabase outage), this bundles everything a logger's device needs to start logging — draw sheet groups, course pars/yardages, camera roster, playoff roster, and generic items — into one file. Send it to a logger's device directly (AirDrop/USB/local Wi-Fi file share, no internet required) and they import it on their Export tab. This is the reverse of a logger sending their shot log back to you.
This is a one-way push of your current Setup data — it does not include shot logs (loggers already have their own export for that, in reverse). Re-export and resend any time Setup changes (e.g. a withdrawal, a new group, updated pars) so loggers pick up the latest version. Importing on a logger's device fully replaces that device's draw sheet/pars/rosters with what's in this file — it's meant for distribution, not merging.

The absolute folder on your Photoshop machine where per-country flag PNGs live (e.g. from your 02A_FLAGS_DATABASE server) — must end without a trailing slash issue (either is fine, it's normalized automatically). Type the path in and click/tab out of this field to save it — it won't apply to any export until it's actually saved here (typing it in chat does not save it into the app). This is a global setting saved once and shared across every event — it will NOT reset or need re-entering when you start a new tournament/event, since it's a fixed folder location, not tournament data. Once saved, every Rounds Payoff AND L3 Info CSV export builds FLAGBOO/FLAGBOOA as <this folder>/<code>.png, using each player's 3-letter nationality (auto-converted from the tour's IOC code to your files' ISO code for the handful of countries where they differ, e.g. MAS→mys, PHI→phl). OOM rank still isn't included in Rounds Payoff, since that layer (Standings_D13) isn't linked as a Photoshop variable in this template. If this field is ever left blank, FLAGBOO/FLAGBOOA export empty — Photoshop won't error on a blank pixel-replacement cell, it silently keeps showing whichever flag image was last loaded for that layer, which can make a completely unrelated country's flag appear on a player's card. A default path is now pre-filled below on every fresh device — if for any reason this field ever appears blank or doesn't seem to save when you type into it, copy this exact path and paste it into the field yourself, then click/tab out to save: /Volumes/ES GEFS_1/00_GFX_Elements/00_Asian Tour Media_Elements/00_2020_2021/17_AT Players_Webpage_071024_Flags_Test

🎞️ EDL — Premiere Pro Rough Assembly Show ▾
Pulls each clip's IN timecode + a short fixed duration onto a rough-assembly sequence, matched to the right camera reel by the operator name set in Camera Roster (falls back to the camera ID if no name is set). Assumes all cameras are jam-synced to the same timecode. Not frame-accurate — just gets the right footage onto the timeline near the right point for trimming.
What to expect in Premiere: on first import, every clip will show as Media Offline \u2014 this is normal, Premiere does not auto-match reel names on import. For each offline clip: right-click \u2192 Link Media... \u2192 uncheck File Name, check Tape Name \u2192 Locate \u2192 point at that operator's clip/folder (Tape Name in Premiere must be set to match the operator's name in Camera Roster, e.g. "Davis", exactly).

Reading the offline clip name: each offline placeholder is named operator_disc_player+shot_timecode \u2014 e.g. davis_disc2_james leow 2a2_14:15:43 means Davis's Disc 2, James Leow's 2nd shot on hole 2, logged around 14:15:43. This is printed right on the clip in the Project panel/Timeline (no need to open the EDL text file) so you can scan an operator's whole bin of similar-looking files and immediately tell which shot each placeholder is for. If disc wasn't noted, that part just says "disc-" \u2014 in that case rely on the timecode instead.

Use that embedded timecode as a guide, not an exact match: pick whichever of the operator's real files has a rolling range that CONTAINS it (clip start \u2264 timecode \u2264 clip end), since loggers react a few seconds after a shot actually starts. Never rely on reel name alone when one operator has more than one file \u2014 the disc number + timecode in the clip name is what actually tells you which physical file to Locate.

🗄️ Archive & Storage Management

Once a tournament has fully wrapped, archive it here: download everything for that event into one JSON file (safe to keep on a drive/HDD), then optionally delete it from Supabase to free up space on the free tier. Nothing is deleted until you type the event name to confirm. If you ever need to look at an archived event again, use Reinstate below to push it back to Supabase.

Reinstate an Archived Event

Pick an archive JSON file (downloaded via "Archive & Download" above) to push that event's data back to Supabase. Safe to run even if some of the data is already there — nothing gets duplicated.
Live per-player accuracy — cards update as shots are logged, showing progress thru N holes. GIR & Putts score every hole that HOLES OUT with a connected shot log — the tee shot need not be logged, since any missing lead-in strokes are retraced from the shot ordinals (a “2nd Shot” onto the green = reached in 2). Only holes still in progress, or with a genuine gap in the log, are excluded. Fairways are read from the tee shot's landing lie, or the 2nd shot's starting lie when logging began there, so a hole logged from the 2nd shot on the fairway counts as a hit. A logger's override to any shot re-traces and recomputes automatically. GIR = on the green in par−2. Putts = strokes started on the green (fringe never counts; de-greening counts each green start). If a round is short, Putts also shows an estimated 18-hole average (putts-per-hole × 18). Fairways = Par 4/5 tee shots that found the fairway.
No holes with a complete shot sequence yet.
Upload each round's tour-supplied Hole-by-Hole (HBH) Excel file (the .xlsx the tour emails, e.g. Yeangder_2026YTPC-HBH-Rd1.xlsx) to compute per-player scoring for the whole field — select all rounds at once and each is auto-filed to its round from the sheet/file name (or pick a round to force a single file). Works fully offline — no internet or live leaderboard needed, so it still works after the tournament ends. Totals are cumulative across every round you import for this event; hot streak is a run of 3+ consecutive birdies‑or‑better (eagles count) in a single round, with the holes shown. Search a player to open their scorecard; use the Sort buttons to surface the most birdies/eagles/bogeys/doubles. Players in your camera roster / draw are highlighted ★. Tip: the Leaderboard (LB) totals file has no per-hole data and is intentionally rejected. OCS fallback: if no Excel is available, the tour's official data partner OCS (apga-apga.ocs-software.com — Tour Information Centre, whose season archive stays live after the event) also works — open its Leaderboard Hole by Hole report, save it as a PDF, and drop it here; it's parsed the same way. This is separate from GIR/Putts/Fairways above, which come only from ATM Logger shot logs.

Connection Settings

Where this device reads/writes shot logs, rosters, chat, and everything else. This is a per-device setting — each phone/tablet/laptop picks its own mode.

Ask whoever started the local server for this address — it prints on their screen when the server starts (e.g. http://192.168.1.23:8787).
Compare record counts between Cloud and Local before switching modes mid-event, so you can confirm nothing was missed on either side.
How Local Network Emergency Mode works Before you travel (test once, ahead of time):
  1. Install Node.js on the laptop that will run the local server (one-time setup).
  2. Click Download Local Server Script (.js) above and save it on that laptop.
  3. Run it: open a terminal in that folder and type node atm-logger-local-server.js. Leave that window open — closing it stops the server.
  4. It will print an address like http://192.168.1.23:8787 — note it down.
On-site, if Supabase is blocked:
  1. Connect the server laptop and every logger's phone/tablet to the same Wi‑Fi network or mobile hotspot.
  2. Start the local server on the laptop (see above) if it isn't already running.
  3. On every device (including the laptop's own browser tab), open this Connection Settings panel, pick Local Network Emergency Mode, enter the laptop's address, and click Test Connection then Save.
  4. Everything — logging, playoff, rosters, chat, playlists, SGFX/PDF exports — keeps working exactly the same, just synced over the local network instead of the internet.
After the event: switch each device back to Cloud once you're somewhere Supabase isn't blocked. Data logged in Local mode stays only on that laptop's server — it does not automatically merge into the cloud project, so keep exporting playlists/PDFs/CSVs as usual before packing up.

📲 Add The Watchtower to Your Home Screen

Installs this app on your tablet/phone so it opens full-screen with its own icon, like any other app — no browser address bar, no re-typing a URL every time. Works with the exact page you're already on, whether that's a hosted link or a local file.

🍎 iPad / iPhone (Safari)
  1. Open this page in Safari (not Chrome — Add to Home Screen only works from Safari on iOS).
  2. Tap the Share icon (square with an arrow pointing up) in the toolbar.
  3. Scroll down and tap Add to Home Screen.
  4. Confirm the name ("Watchtower") and tap Add (top-right).
  5. The golf-flag icon now appears on your home screen — tap it to launch full-screen, no browser bar.
🤖 Android Tablet/Phone (Chrome)
  1. Open this page in Chrome.
  2. Tap the ⋮ menu (top-right corner).
  3. Tap Add to Home screen (or Install app if Chrome offers it directly).
  4. Confirm the name and tap Add / Install.
  5. The golf-flag icon now appears on your home screen — tap it to launch full-screen, no browser bar.
Do this once per device, on whichever copy of the file/link you're using that day — if a newer version is distributed later, reinstalling (same steps) replaces the shortcut with the latest one. Local Network Emergency Mode and offline logging both keep working exactly the same after installing.
